note: Both sets contain essentially the same 18 claims in different order, so neither is substantively better. Each correctly captures the composition ranges, phase structures, 4-5% strain, 2-5% typical contraction, 25-50C hysteresis and 15-30C engineered transition temperature. However, each also repeats the same two misread claims (hysteresis '20-50C' and force 'upwards of 20,000 PSI', both contradicting the page's 25-50C and 25,000 PSI) and each duplicates the nickel, titanium, contraction and strain facts under two names.
remarks: Both extractions appear to be the same claim pool with reordering; the '20-50C' and '20,000 PSI' claims are fabricated variants of the page's 25-50C and 25,000 PSI values and their quotes do not match the text layer. Both sets also carry contradictory pairs (25,000 vs 20,000 PSI; 25-50C vs 20-50C). Facts on the page both sets miss: discovery of Nitinol in 1961, the Nitinol-actuated linear diffuser application, and the hysteresis-induced lag/delayed relaxation behavior.
